transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I can't tell you exactly which part to buy yet because 'not draining' after a clean filter usually comes down to one of two things: either there's still a blockage somewhere in the hose system (the drain hose or your household waste pipe), or the pump itself has failed. To separate these, please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin' programme and listen at the bottom front while it tries to empty. Do you hear the pump humming/buzzing (which suggests a blockage) or is it silent (suggesting a faulty pump)? Also, quickly check that the drain hose isn't kinked.
Pump hums but the water doesn't move. Hose behind looks fine, no kinks. So is it the pump then?

To answer your question directly: not necessarily. A humming pump that doesn't move water usually means the motor is trying to work but can't turn because something is jammed in the impeller (the fan inside), or less commonly, the motor itself has burnt out. Before you buy a new pump, please do this quick check: with the machine switched off and unplugged, look into the filter hole. Can you see the plastic impeller blades? Try to spin them gently with your finger. If they are stuck or you feel something hard blocking them, that is likely the problem (and might just need clearing out). If they spin freely but it still won't drain when running, then the pump motor itself has probably failed and needs replacing.
Did that - impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. Also E18 comes up on the display when it stalls. So is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
To answer your question directly: yes, it is probably the drain pump. However, I cannot give you a specific part number yet because 'FD 9409' does not match a standard Bosch model format in my system (it may be a series code or a typo). To get the correct pump, please check the full model number on the rating plate inside the door rim or on the back of the machine��it usually starts with something like WGA, WAQ, or SMS followed by numbers and letters. Once you have that, you can order the part yourself if you are comfortable replacing it (it involves removing the top and rear panels), or call an engineer to do it safely.

FD 9409 is off the sticker inside the door, that's what it says. The E-Nr line next to it is rubbed off so I can't read it. Front just says Bosch Serie 4 and VarioPerfect. Can you work out the pump from that?

I cannot work out the specific pump part number from 'FD 9409' alone because that code does not uniquely identify a single Bosch washing machine model in my system. Without the full model number (usually starting with WGA, WAQ, etc.) and the E-Nr (which is rubbed off), I risk giving you the wrong part. Since you cannot confirm the exact model to order the correct replacement, I recommend contacting Bosch Customer Support with the serial number (if visible) or calling a qualified engineer who can identify the part on-site and fit it safely.
